actions: flexes, abducts, externally rotates hip; flexes knee -- the classic 'cross-legged tailor's-seat' combined action

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Longest muscle in the human body, crossing both the hip and knee diagonally; its very long parallel fascicles (essentially spanning its full length) are architecturally suited to large-excursion, low-force multi-joint motion rather than strength.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the middle third of the medial thigh. For injection, the proximal third and the distal third of the anteromedial thigh, matching the muscle's two arborization zones.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: The most superficial structure of the medial thigh, lying over vastus medialis and the adductors, which in turn lie on the femoral cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Two injection sites follow directly from the two zones at 20-40% and 60-80%.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

trigger_points.location_description: Superficial, along the course of the muscle from the anterior superior iliac spine obliquely across the anterior thigh toward the medial knee; trigger points here rarely occur in isolation
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A sharp, superficial burning or tingling sensation felt directly along the path of the muscle itself, rather than at a distance, most notable over the anteromedial thigh and medial knee
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Almost always occurs as a satellite to trigger points in other hip/thigh muscles (iliopsoas, tensor fasciae latae, quadriceps, adductors) rather than as a primary, isolated finding
trigger_points.notes: Travell & Simons nickname sartorius the 'surreptitious accomplice' because its own trigger points are rarely a primary complaint and its referred sensation is unusually superficial and confined to the muscle's course rather than forming a discrete distant zone
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in Niel Asher Education, 'Trigger Point Therapy | Sartorius Muscle' (https://nielasher.com/blogs/video-blog/trigger-point-therapy-sartorius)
